description: 5K runner hits a prescribed tempo session. Dean should compare actual pace to prescribed pace explicitly and tie it to race prep — not give generic feedback.

user.name: Marcus
user.notes: Training for a local 5K, goal sub-21min.

ground_truth.notes: Marcus's prescribed tempo is 4mi (1mi WU + 2mi @ 7:54/mi + 1mi CD). He ran 4.1mi with splits: 9:42 (WU), 7:58, 7:55 (tempo segments), 9:50 (CD). The tempo segments averaged 7:57/mi vs prescribed 7:54/mi — essentially on target (3 sec/mile over). Dean MUST explicitly compare actual vs prescribed pace: e.g. 'The tempo miles came in at 7:57/mi — right on your 7:54 target, essentially a perfect execution.' The insight must also connect to 5K race prep. Dean MUST NOT just say 'great tempo run' without comparing to prescribed pace. The 9:42 WU and 9:50 CD should be read as intentional warmup/cooldown, not pacing anomalies. The overall average (8:10/mi) is diluted by the WU/CD — do not use the overall pace as the tempo benchmark.
